title: Scrolling horizontally and vertically on a grid pager work in an unexpected way
line: Scrolling sideways over a pager with several rows now stays in the current row instead of jumping to the next one.
explanation: The pager's wheel handler took the vertical or horizontal delta and stepped linearly through the whole desktop list, so on a grid a sideways scroll from the end of one row moved to the start of the next, even with "Navigation wraps around" off. The change makes horizontal scrolling work only within the current row (clamped, or wrapping inside the row when wrap-around is on). Vertical scrolling keeps stepping through every desktop, so a plain mouse wheel can still reach all of them.

commits.message:
applets/pager: Keep horizontal scrolling within the current row

On a pager with several rows, scrolling sideways stepped through all
desktops and jumped to the next row, even with wrapping off. Keep it in
the current row; vertical scrolling still reaches every desktop.

BUG: 471160

media.caption: 4 desktops in 2 rows, wrap-around off: on desktop 2 one notch of horizontal scroll to the right jumps to desktop 3 in the next row.
Same notch with the fix: it stays on desktop 2, the end of its row.

review.text: Keeping horizontal scrolling within the current row while letting vertical scrolling traverse every desktop is a reasonable UX compromise for standard mouse wheels, and the screenshots verify the single-notch horizontal mouse-wheel case. However, the patch has a multi-notch loop bug (const current is calculated outside the while loop), fails to handle horizontal two-finger touchpad scrolling (which typically carries slight non-zero angleDelta.y), and uses BUG: 471160 even though the vertical-scrolling half of the report is intentionally left unaddressed.
changes: Change BUG: 471160 to CCBUG: 471160 in the commit message, since vertical grid scrolling (Expected Result #1 in the bug report) is intentionally left unchanged.

Update current across iterations of the while (increment !== 0) loop (or compute the final target page and call pagerModel.changePage() once) so fast scrolls with Math.abs(increment) > 1 do not repeatedly call changePage() with the same stale page.

Decide horizontal vs. vertical scrolling by comparing Math.abs(wheel.angleDelta.x) > Math.abs(wheel.angleDelta.y) (and avoid mixing x and y deltas in the same root.wheelDelta accumulator) so horizontal two-finger touchpad swipes with slight vertical jitter stay within the current row.
